page: Amazon Web Services r7i.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for vector and matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2154.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.68 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8098.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 7070.01. Memory bandwidth is measured at 689.3 GB/sec for cached small blocks and approximately 52.25 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. For specialized tasks, the instance achieves 10.88 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 14.83 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, text generation for medium-sized 7B language models is a relative bottleneck, registering at 7.97 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7i.2xlarge offers high memory density with DDR5 technology, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The lack of bundled local storage means users must rely on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy operations. The instance is suited for database operations, memory-intensive applications, text processing, and software compilation. It is less optimal for large-scale LLM text generation or workloads requiring local high-speed scratch space.
